extracted.intended_audience: novelists, creative-writing students, literary critics and scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and prescriptive criteria for composing serious literary fiction (particularly the novel), emphasizing representation of life, observation, specificity, and artistic freedom. Drawn from Henry James's 1884 essay arguing against prescriptive craft rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest as the only obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The only obligation to which in advance we may hold a novel, without incurring the accusation of being arbitrary, is that it be interesting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'interesting' as the primary non-arbitrary rule: a work must engage attention and curiosity. This is not a prescription of specific devices, but a guiding standard against which other choices are judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of life
rubrics_metrics.description: "The only reason for the existence of a novel is that it does attempt to represent life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction's purpose is to depict human experience and social reality with fidelity and complexity; novels should aim to capture life rather than merely amuse or instruct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute freedom of subject and method
rubrics_metrics.description: "The novelist must have absolute freedom to choose subject and method."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject externally imposed prescriptions about what subject matter or narrative techniques are 'proper'; artistic choices should be governed by the work's needs and the writer's vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination counts as experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "Experience is never limited... it is an immense sensibility... catching every air-borne particle in its tissue." (Imagination as valid form of experience.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not privilege only lived events as source material—imaginative empathy and mental receptivity are legitimate grounds for creating authentic fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: The novelist's eye / observant sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Try to be one of the people on whom nothing is lost!" (The novelist's first quality is observation.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate acute attention to detail and nuance; perception of small, telling particulars is essential to rendering life convincingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solidity of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel's "merit lies in the very intensity with which it has been felt." The writer must achieve "solidity of specification" — concrete, sense-grounded representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor concrete, sensory, and specific detail over vague generality; specificity lends credibility and emotional force to characterization and scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of character and incident
rubrics_metrics.description: "What is character but the determination of incident? What is incident but the illustration of character?" (Plot and character are inseparable.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure incidents grow naturally from character motivations and that character is revealed through action; avoid treating plot and character as opposed elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of mind / avoidance of superficiality
rubrics_metrics.description: "No good novel will ever proceed from a superficial mind..." (Moral quality follows from depth, not imposed lessons.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for psychological and intellectual depth; moral seriousness should emerge from the work's complexity rather than didactic statements or simplistic moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity of feeling and insight
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should exhibit the "intensity with which it has been felt."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author's engagement—emotional and intellectual intensity—should be evident in the writing, producing conviction and resonance for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive perception ('miss nothing')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for thoroughness of perception: notice and render subtle, overlooked elements of situation and character so the fiction feels complete and alive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of prescriptive craft rules
rubrics_metrics.description: James rejects "rules about what fiction must include or exclude."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid strict, formulaic checklists prescribing content, structure, or technique; evaluate choices on how well they serve interest and truthful representation rather than on adherence to rules.
